title: Prospective Clinical Study for the Validation and Optimization of Diagnostic Methods for Chronic Periprosthetic Joint Infections
summary:
This study aims to enhance the safety and reliability of diagnosing chronic prosthetic joint infections including the causative agents. To achieve this, we intend to include all patients presenting to our clinic with suspected chronic periprosthetic infection. No additional examinations (such as blood sampling, joint aspiration, or radiography) will be performed solely for study purposes. Instead, where possible, additional material (blood, synovial fluid) will be collected as part of the standard diagnostic procedures that are strictly indicated for medical reasons. From these additional samples, novel laboratory parameters will be assessed, and molecular genetic pathogen identification will be conducted.

The insights gained from this study could help improve the accuracy of diagnosing chronic prosthetic joint infections and enhance the identification of causative pathogens. This, in turn, may enable more targeted antibiotic therapy.

Furthermore, the study aims to improve the safety and reliability of infection control before prosthesis reimplantation in two-stage revision procedures. For this purpose, we plan to include all patients diagnosed with a chronic periprosthetic infection who have undergone prosthesis removal and are scheduled for reimplantation as part of a staged revision. These patients will undergo the same study diagnostics again before or during the reimplantation procedure.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal joint prosthesis

interventions.name:
Infection Confirmed (Case Group)
- Diagnostic cascade in suspected chronic periprosthetic infection, consisting of systemic blood laboratory analysis and joint aspiration, including routine and study-specific diagnostics.
- Collection and evaluation of standardized routine questionnaires.
- Asses

Infection ruled out (Control group)
- Diagnostic cascade in suspected chronic periprosthetic infection, consisting of systemic blood laboratory testing and joint aspiration analysis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Capacity to Consent
- Treatment Diagnosis: Suspected PJI of knee or hip 
- Treatment Period: March 1, 2025, until the minimum case number is reached or for a maximum of 18–24 months (as stated above)
- Surgical Site: Orthopedic University Hospital Heidelberg
Exclusion criteria:
- Periprosthetic infection of another joint
- Infection of a native joint
- Infection of soft tissues, bone, or osteosynthetic material without involvement of an - - implanted prosthesis
- Revision of a prosthesis due to another cause (e.g., aseptic loosening, etc.)
- Lack of consent capability or consent form from participants
